title: Dundee Cake
subtitle: Rich Scottish fruit cake topped with whole almonds
excerpt: Scotland's most famous export cake: a rich, moist fruit cake flavoured with orange, studded with dried fruit and currants, and topped with concentric rings of whole blanched almonds. Made for keeping.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dundee cake originated in the Dundee marmalade industry of the nineteenth century. The most commonly cited origin story attributes it to James Keiller, whose family established a marmalade factory in Dundee in the early nineteenth century; the cake is said to have used the orange peel by-product of the marmalade process. Whatever its precise origins, Dundee cake became Scotland's most recognisable cake internationally, distinguished from the richer Christmas cake by a lighter fruit load, the inclusion of orange zest, and the characteristic topping of whole blanched almonds arranged in concentric rings. It is meant to be eaten without icing, as a cut-and-come-again cake that keeps well in a tin.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 20 cm round cake tin, greased and lined with baking paper.

content.text: Add the eggs one at a time and beat well between each addition to prevent the batter from splitting. If it looks curdled, add a tablespoon of flour with the next egg. The batter should be thick enough to drop slowly from the spoon. The almond topping is a distinctive feature: arrange them carefully in neat concentric rings before baking and brush with milk so they brown evenly.

Heat the oven to 160 C (140 C fan). Grease and double-line a deep 20 cm round tin with baking paper, with the paper coming 3 cm above the rim. Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, adding a tablespoon of flour with each egg after the first.

Fold in the remaining flour, mixed spice, and baking powder. Stir in all the dried fruit, mixed peel, orange zest, and lemon zest until evenly distributed. The batter will be thick. Spoon into the prepared tin and level the surface.

Arrange the blanched almonds in concentric circles over the top of the cake. Brush lightly with milk. Bake for 1.5 hours until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Check after 1 hour and cover with foil if the top is browning too quickly. Cool completely in the tin before turning out. Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 2 weeks.
